subject: Anthropology
title: Kinship Terminology
description: A quick win: understand Kinship Terminology.

hook.text: English has one word for cousin. Some languages have eight. Your kinship vocabulary shapes how you see your family.

buildup.text: Kinship terminology systems classify relatives into categories, and each system reflects different social priorities.

discovery.text: There are six major systems: Hawaiian, Eskimo, Sudanese, Omaha, Crow, and Iroquois, each grouping relatives differently.

twist.text: Terminology isn't just labels. Calling someone 'brother' versus 'cousin' changes your obligations toward them.

climax.text: Kinship terms reveal hidden social logic. They show who matters, who helps, and who you must respect or avoid.

punchline.text: How you name relatives shapes how you treat them.

quiz.question: Why do kinship terminology systems matter?
options: They shape social obligations and reveal who matters in a society
They only exist in written languages

details.summary: Different cultures use distinct terminology systems to classify relatives. Anthropologists identified major systems — Eskimo, Hawaiian, Iroquois, Sudanese, Crow, and Omaha — each reflecting different principles of social organization and descent.
details.whyItMatters: Kinship terminology reveals how a culture categorizes social relationships. The words people use for relatives encode cultural priorities about lineage, marriage, and social distinction.
takeaways: Six major kinship terminology systems have been identified globally
Each system reflects underlying principles of social organization
Terminology shapes how people perceive and act toward relatives

faq.question: What is the Eskimo kinship terminology system?
faq.answer: The Eskimo system, used in most Western societies, distinguishes nuclear family members (mother, father, brother, sister) from all other relatives who are grouped as aunts, uncles, and cousins regardless of side. It emphasizes the nuclear family unit.

faq.question: How does kinship terminology affect behavior?
faq.answer: In many cultures, using the same kinship term for multiple relatives means treating them similarly. If your father's brother is called 'father,' you may owe him the same respect and obedience as your biological father.
